history.period: 1986 (Central Gangging) / 1989 (first major Donyi-Polo temple), both at Pasighat
history.summary: NON-HINDU RECORD FLAG (kept with flag per project convention): Donyi-Polo is the indigenous animist faith of the Tani tribes (Adi, Galo, Tagin, Nyishi, Apatani) of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, not Hinduism. Donyi = Sun (female, 'Ane Donyi' = Mother Sun) and Polo = Moon (male, 'Abo Polo' = Father Moon); Wikipedia's Donyi-Polo religion article notes 'The first major Donyi-Polo temple was built by Talom Rukbo at Pasighat in 1989' and that by the mid-2010s the network had grown to around four hundred centres. A 'gangging' is the Donyi-Polo prayer place/prayer hall - an institution created for the Donyi-Polo Yelam Kebang (founded 31 December 1986; that date is celebrated as Donyi-Polo Day), with the Central Gangging constructed in Pasighat in 1986 per Scheid (Internationales Asienforum, Heidelberg, 2015). Sunday prayers are the weekly cycle and village ganggings are centrally regulated by the Yelam Kebang. Talom Rukbo (founder of the revival; 20-ft statue unveiled at Pasighat by the Governor in October 2018, per Arunachal Governor press release) established the institutional movement here, so this Pasighat gangging is the faith's central prayer place. LOCATION FLAG: the exact street address of the 1986/1989 temple is not published; the nearby Donyi Polo Vidya Niketan stands at Talom Rukbo Nagar, Pasighat (approx 28.0615, 95.3297), and the temple is associated with that complex. Coordinates are Pasighat town centre, marked approximate. IMAGE SEARCH FAILURE: no verifiable image of the Pasighat Donyi-Polo temple exists, so media is empty.

town_description: Pasighat is the headquarters of East Siang district, Arunachal Pradesh, set on the Siang (Brahmaputra) river ~45 km from Assam. One of the state's oldest towns and the heart of Adi country, it hosts the Adi Baane Kebang headquarters, the Donyi-Polo Yelam Kebang institutions (including Donyi Polo Vidya Niketan at Talom Rukbo Nagar), the East Siang District Museum, and Pasighat Airport (military airstrip with civilian use).
